name: CA-38
label: Safe D

key_factors: Post-redistricting district leans Democratic by about eight points on the PVI
Hilda Solis holds a large fundraising edge with outside support and no outside opposition
Prediction markets price the Democratic candidate near 98 percent
No general-election polls or expert ratings, so the forecast rests on fundamentals
model.rationale: The fundamentals point clearly Democratic: the redrawn district carries an eight-point Democratic lean, a favorable national environment adds to it, and Solis has raised over a million dollars while Casas reports minimal resources. Markets price this as a near-certain Democratic hold, consistent with a Safe D rating.
model.watch: Low-turnout special-election dynamics or a surge of consolidated Republican spending could narrow the margin, though not enough to plausibly flip the seat.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; fundamentals point clearly one way (post-redistricting), so it is treated as safe for that party.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
This open Southern California seat was redrawn after the 2020 cycle and now carries an eight-point Democratic lean, making the party a clear favorite to elect a new representative. Former supervisor and labor leader Hilda Solis enters with strong name recognition, more than a million dollars raised, and outside groups supporting her, while Republican Pedro Casas reports little visible fundraising or outside backing.

With no public polls and no expert ratings of the race, the forecast leans on district fundamentals and market pricing, both of which point the same way. A comfortable Democratic win is expected, with the main uncertainty being the size of the margin rather than the outcome.
